verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “over the last few weeks or so… I don't have much energy at all during the day” and later clarifies duration: “More like two months, I would say. Yeah.”
Patient reports difficulty getting up: “I don't really feel like getting up in the morning is really difficult…,” and later confirms duration “More like two months, I would say. Yeah.”

Patient states, “I'm not eating very much at the moment,” and the discussion of symptoms spans “maybe… a couple of months ago” and “More like two months, I would say,” supporting decreased appetite over about 2 months.
When asked about mornings, patient replies, “I'm just not normally waking up early. It's more like I'm just having trouble sleeping at all.”
Patient states, “Finding it really hard to. Quite difficult to keep focusing.”
Patient adds, “I would say not unhappy or happy, but just quite. Just not focused,” and clinician paraphrases, “difficulty focusing, quite distracted,” indicating easy distractibility.
Patient says, “my mood is lower recently,” and context around “over the last few months” ties this to a few-month period.
Patient reports, “my mood is lower recently and so I Like my sex drive has kind of decreased over the past few months as well,” and later, “just over the last few months, just been disinterested.”

Patient initially says, “I haven't noticed anything like that specifically,” then clarifies, “Yeah, I don't think it's an important change. No… No, there hasn't been a change there,” indicating no noticed change in morning erections.

Patient states, “when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe. So I have some kind of like shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago.”
Patient reports, “I have a history of hypothyroidism… Hypo Hypothyroidism… Hypo Hypo.” Clinician confirms, “Okay. Hypothyroid. Thank you.”
Patient says, “I have a drug history of thyroxine…,” and when asked, “Do you continue to take thyroxine now?” replies, “Yes… So you're taking thyroxine at the moment? Yes.”
When asked, “Are you allergic to any medications?” patient answers, “No, I have no medication. Allergies?” Clinician summarizes, “No allergies.”
Patient states, “my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago.”

Clinician asks about other family history: “Is there any other significant family history… No, no depression or anything like that? Running in family or. Okay. And your mother is as well? Any brothers or sisters?” Patient replies, “Yeah, she's fine and I'm an early child,” so no other psychiatric/familial illness is reported.
In response to relationship status, patient says, “Yeah, I'm married. I've been for many years.”
The transcript contains no physical examination findings; the clinician explicitly plans a future in‑person exam: “I would like to probably see you in person and do an examination.”

Clinician groups mood and energy symptoms: “More fatigue, more shortness of breath over the last few months with a lower mood, decreased sex drive,” and asks about suicidality and enjoyment of activities, consistent with assessing fatigue/low mood as depressive symptoms.
Transcript notes hypothyroidism and thyroxine use but does not state that thyroid control status “should be considered”; this is an added interpretive plan not explicitly mentioned.

Patient describes exertional dyspnea: “when I've been doing sports… it's quite difficult to breathe… shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago,” and clinician restates, “you've become more short of breath over the last few months.”

Clinician says, “I would like to probably see you in person and do an examination… do you think it'd be possible to… book an appointment in the next few days with your GP… and then we could… do an examination.”

Clinician states, “I would like to… do an examination and also we probably like to do some blood tests as well… and do some investigations, really, to see what's going on,” which includes labs such as thyroid function given known hypothyroidism, a direct clinical inference.

While mood and suicidality are discussed (“some people… can sometimes feel suicidal… Have you had any thoughts…?”), there is no explicit plan stated to ‘monitor mood symptoms and assess for depression and support needs’ beyond arranging GP follow‑up.
Clinician advises, “do you think it'd be possible to… book an appointment in the next few days with your GP… That would be ideal,” indicating follow‑up in primary care within days.
